title: Acyclicity of successive direct image on K-injectives
statement: Let f:X→Y and g:Y→Z be morphisms of ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Let I be any unbounded K-injective complex of O_X-modules [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Write Q for localization of homotopy categories. With the module direct images and right-derived units of [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], the component η_g(f_* I):Q(g_* f_* I)→Rg_*(Q(f_* I)) is an isomorphism. No flatness, boundedness, or K-injectivity of f_* I is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0D5S and 079W; the argument of Tag 0D5T restricted to K-injective representatives, including compatibility of derived and underived adjunctions

proof.text: Choose K-flat resolutions using lem-pc-kflat-resolution. The termwise tensor pullbacks of g, then f, preserve K-flatness by lem-pc-kflat-pullback-preservation. On a K-flat resolution of an object of D(O_Z), the composite left derived pullback is consequently represented by f^*g^* of that resolution. The underived sectionwise tensor pullback composition isomorphism identifies this with (g∘f)^* of the same resolution; both compute the composite-morphism left derived pullback. The comparison is natural because the tensor pullback identification is natural on complexes and the derived functor comparison is characterized by its counit. This constructs the ringed-space pullback comparison directly; the existing scheme-only Lean pullback-composition statement is not assumed.

Apply lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint-general for f, g, and g∘f. For every object E of D(O_Z), the composite adjunction identifies Hom(Lf^*Lg^* E,QI) with Hom(E,Rg_*Rf_*QI); the adjunction for the composite identifies Hom(L(g∘f)^*E,QI) with Hom(E,R(g∘f)_*QI). The previous pullback comparison identifies their left sides, naturally in E. Yoneda therefore identifies the right adjoints evaluated at QI. Compatibility of the derived adjunction with its underived unit/counit identifies this Yoneda map with the map induced by the pasted right-derived units on I: first η_g(f_*I), then Rg_*η_f(I), with the sectionwise composition identification. This is the mate calculation of Tags 079W and 0D5T, performed only at I.

Since I is K-injective, η_f(I) and η_(g∘f)(I) are invertible by the K-injective computation of the defining right derived functors. The Yoneda comparison is invertible by the preceding Hom bijections. Hence the composite η_g(f_*I) followed by Rg_*η_f(I) is invertible. Its second factor is invertible because functors preserve isomorphisms; cancelling this factor proves that η_g(f_*I) is invertible. This conclusion concerns only the unit on the specified complexes, not preservation of K-injectivity under module direct image.
